title: Are You Ignoring These Burnout Warning Signs? Psychologist Warnings.

sentences.en: Sometimes we get so used to doing things a certain way that we forget there might be other possibilities.
sentences.zh: 有时候我们太习惯于某种做事方式，以至于忘记了可能还有其他选择。

sentences.en: That can most definitely apply to our working lives too.
sentences.zh: 这一点绝对也适用于我们的工作生活。

sentences.en: I'm Dr Marianne Trent and one of the biggest changes I've made in my career has been exploring ways to earn money beyond traditional one-to-one work.
sentences.zh: 我是 Marianne Trent 博士，我职业生涯中做出的最大改变之一，就是探索传统一对一工作之外的赚钱方式。

sentences.en: If that sparks your curiosity, Sophie Foote's free Race to Recurring
sentences.zh: 如果这激发了你的好奇心，Sophie Foote 的免费“Race to Recurring”

sentences.en: Revenue Challenge starts on the 2nd of November.
sentences.zh: 收入挑战赛将于 11 月 2 日开始。

sentences.en: I'd love you to join us.
sentences.zh: 我很乐意你加入我们。

sentences.en: You'll find my link in the show notes or you can drop me a DM via socials.
sentences.zh: 你可以在节目说明中找到我的链接，或者通过社交媒体给我发私信。

sentences.en: Now on with the show.
sentences.zh: 现在继续我们的节目。

sentences.en: People talk about the sweet spot of work-life balance but what if that is hard to achieve?
sentences.zh: 人们常谈论工作与生活平衡的“甜蜜点”，但如果这很难实现呢？

sentences.en: What if both of those pressures feel like they are meaning that you are heading towards burnout?
sentences.zh: 如果这两种压力让你感觉自己正走向倦怠呢？

sentences.en: Let's take a deep dive looking at all of the different types of factors that can contribute to you or someone you care about feeling burned out.
sentences.zh: 让我们深入探讨一下，导致你或你关心的人感到倦怠的所有不同类型的因素。

sentences.en: I hope you find it so useful.
sentences.zh: 希望你觉得这非常有用。

sentences.en: Hi welcome along to the Aspiring Psychologist podcaSt. I am Dr
sentences.zh: 嗨，欢迎收听《Aspiring Psychologist》播客。我是

sentences.en: Marianne Trent and I'm a qualified clinical psychologiSt. For the last five episodes I have been bringing you
sentences.zh: Marianne Trent 博士，我是一名合格的临床心理学家。在过去五期节目中，我一直为你带来

sentences.en: a special special special series on burnout or more specifically what burnout is and how to avoid it
sentences.zh: 一个关于倦怠的特别系列，更具体地说，是关于什么是倦怠以及如何避免它，

sentences.en: both for yourself for those that you might be working with and or those you care about.
sentences.zh: 无论是为你自己，还是为你可能共事的人或你关心的人。

sentences.en: It has been my pleasure to work alongside Dr Claire Plumley who is also a qualified clinical psychologist and the author of a brilliant new book on burnout.
sentences.zh: 我很高兴能与 Claire Plumley 博士合作，她也是一位合格的临床心理学家，并撰写了一本关于倦怠的精彩新书。

sentences.en: We have evidenced during this series that teamwork makes the dream work and it's always okay to have people support you.
sentences.zh: 我们在本系列中证明了团队合作能成就梦想，寻求他人的支持永远没问题。

sentences.en: You don't need to worry about me.
sentences.zh: 你不需要担心我。

sentences.en: I'm not going anywhere.
sentences.zh: 我哪儿也不会去。

sentences.en: It's just that over the summer it can be a little bit of a juggle with the children.
sentences.zh: 只是在夏天，照顾孩子可能会让人有点手忙脚乱。

sentences.en: I wanted to make sure I was still providing you super brilliant useful content whenever you are ready to listen or watch it.
sentences.zh: 我想确保无论你何时准备收听或观看，我都能为你提供超级精彩且有用的内容。

sentences.en: Claire is really spoiling us with our final installment of the burnout bites.
sentences.zh: Claire 在我们“倦怠小贴士”的最后一期节目中真的让我们大饱耳福。

sentences.en: Absolutely don't need to have listened to the previous five episodes but I would recommend that you do because they are exceptional.
sentences.zh: 你绝对不需要听过前五期节目，但我建议你听一下，因为它们非常出色。

sentences.en: Let's dive in and hear our final burnout bite with Dr Claire.
sentences.zh: 让我们开始吧，听听 Claire 博士带来的最后一期“倦怠小贴士”。

sentences.en: Hello and welcome to the final of burnout bites.
sentences.zh: 你好，欢迎来到“倦怠小贴士”的最后一期。

sentences.en: This has been a series of six short episodes that I've brought to you all about this
sentences.zh: 这是一个由六集短片组成的系列节目，我为大家带来了关于

sentences.en: topic of burnout in the hope that we can understand it and take collective action to looking after ourselves and protecting those around us as well.
sentences.zh: 倦怠这一主题的内容，希望我们能理解它，并采取集体行动来照顾好自己，同时也保护我们周围的人。

sentences.en: I'm Dr Claire Plumley.
sentences.zh: 我是 Claire Plumley 博士。

sentences.en: I am a clinical psychologiSt.
sentences.zh: 我是一名临床心理学家。

sentences.en: I work with people who have experienced trauma and are feeling anxious or burnt out and I have a
sentences.zh: 我与经历过创伤并感到焦虑或倦怠的人一起工作，我有一个

sentences.en: clinical practice both online and in Taunton Somerset and I have recently written a book.
sentences.zh: 在线以及在萨默塞特郡汤顿的临床诊所，我最近写了一本书。

sentences.en: The book's called Burnout, How to Manage Your Nervous System Before It Manages You.
sentences.zh: 书名是《倦怠：在神经系统掌控你之前如何掌控它》。

sentences.en: The link is in the show notes and a lot of the nuggets I've brought to you over this short series has been from that.
sentences.zh: 链接在节目说明里，我在这个短系列中带给你的很多干货都来自这本书。

sentences.en: So today I wanted to bring you this idea of the difference between external and internal pressures because
sentences.zh: 所以今天我想带给大家这个关于外部压力和内部压力之间区别的想法，因为

sentences.en: on the surface you'd think it would be simple if we're feeling stressed that we would slow down and
sentences.zh: 从表面上看，你会觉得很简单，如果我们感到压力，我们应该放慢速度，

sentences.en: pace ourselves and pause and rest so that we don't then tip into this more closed out overwhelmed burnt out place.
sentences.zh: 调整节奏，暂停和休息，这样我们就不会陷入这种封闭、不知所措、倦怠的状态。

sentences.en: But there are two reasons that we don't.
sentences.zh: 但我们没有这样做有两个原因。

sentences.en: There are external pressures that come from the people and situations around us and there are internal pressures that come from within us.
sentences.zh: 有来自我们周围的人和环境的外部压力，也有来自我们内心的内部压力。

sentences.en: So
sentences.zh: 所以

sentences.en: I'm going to break that down today so you have a little bit more of an understanding of it.
sentences.zh: 我今天会把这一点拆解开来，让你对它有更多的了解。

sentences.en: External pressures includes the types of demands in our lives that are really hard to escape from.
sentences.zh: 外部压力包括我们生活中那些真的很难逃避的需求类型。

sentences.en: So it's the boring adulting type of things that we have to just get on and do unfortunately.
sentences.zh: 所以，这就是那些不幸的是我们必须硬着头皮去做的无聊的成年人琐事。

sentences.en: So bills to pay, high caseload, dependents like children or elderly parents.
sentences.zh: 比如要支付的账单、繁重的工作量、像孩子或年迈父母这样的受抚养人。

sentences.en: It might be quarterly targets or questions and wants from the people in our lives who we really care about.
sentences.zh: 这可能是季度目标，或者是我们生活中真正关心的人提出的要求和愿望。

sentences.en: The thing with these external pressures is that sometimes they're super obvious but sometimes there's a little chipping away effect that can go on.
sentences.zh: 这些外部压力的问题在于，有时它们非常明显，但有时会有一种持续的、一点点蚕食的效果。

sentences.en: They can just start to mount up.
sentences.zh: 它们可能会开始堆积起来。

sentences.en: And when I worked in my NHS job, this happened in a really gradual way.
sentences.zh: 当我在 NHS 工作时，这种情况就是以一种非常渐进的方式发生的。

sentences.en: And often on their own, each little demand felt almost inconsequential.
sentences.zh: 而且通常单独来看，每一个小小的需求都显得几乎无关紧要。

sentences.en: And like I would be creating a bit of a fuss if I said anything about this.
sentences.zh: 而且我觉得如果我对此说三道四，好像是我在小题大做。

sentences.en: So for example, when I first started to work in the NHS, as a full time equivalent, you're expected to see about 15 clients a week.
sentences.zh: 例如，当我刚开始在 NHS 工作时，作为全职员工，你预计每周要见大约 15 位客户。

sentences.en: When I left that position, which was almost seven years later, a full time equivalent was expected to see 25 clients in a week.
sentences.zh: 当我离开那个职位时，那已经是近七年之后了，全职员工预计每周要见 25 位客户。

sentences.en: Not only that, but we were expected to do measures at each session and provide more reports.
sentences.zh: 不仅如此，我们还被要求在每次会话中进行评估并提供更多报告。

sentences.en: It was just a lot.
sentences.zh: 这真的太多了。

sentences.en: And it hadn't become quite clear to me until I sat down and really thought about it, how much more I was being asked to do.
sentences.zh: 直到我坐下来认真思考时，我才清楚地意识到，我被要求做的事情多了多少。

sentences.en: So here's a list of the common external pressures.
sentences.zh: 所以这里有一份常见的外部压力清单。

sentences.en: So you can just check in and see how many of these you've got going on.
sentences.zh: 你可以对照一下，看看你有多少种情况。

sentences.en: Holding in mind that this won't just be at work, this will be in your personal life and friendship life and any maybe voluntary commitments that you have as well.
sentences.zh: 请记住，这不仅仅是在工作中，这也会发生在你的个人生活、友谊生活以及你可能有的任何志愿承诺中。

sentences.en: So take it as a broad brushstroke.
sentences.zh: 所以把它当作一个广泛的概括。

sentences.en: Time pressures.
sentences.zh: 时间压力。

sentences.en: So this might be deadlines, completing projects, or you know, on a day to day basis where you've got to get somewhere at a certain time, get the kids to a club at a certain time.
sentences.zh: 这可能是截止日期、完成项目，或者你知道，在日常生活中，你必须在特定时间到达某个地方，在特定时间把孩子送到俱乐部。

sentences.en: Any conflicts or disagreement where you're kind of feeling this constant pressure of being up against someone else or friction.
sentences.zh: 任何冲突或分歧，让你感到一种与他人对抗或摩擦的持续压力。

sentences.en: Any high emotional labour in your job.
sentences.zh: 工作中任何高强度的情感劳动。

sentences.en: So tending to others and negative emotions, and not having emotional support for your own.
sentences.zh: 即照顾他人的负面情绪，而自己的情绪却得不到支持。

sentences.en: This is a really strong external pressure that can be a bit more invisible.
sentences.zh: 这是一种非常强大的外部压力，可能更隐蔽一些。

sentences.en: Workload, just having too much to do.
sentences.zh: 工作量，就是要做的事情太多了。

sentences.en: And obviously that ties in with the time pressure, often not enough time to do it.
sentences.zh: 显然这与时间压力有关，通常没有足够的时间来完成。

sentences.en: This is an interesting one.
sentences.zh: 这是一个有趣的点。

sentences.en: Role ambiguity.
sentences.zh: 角色模糊。

sentences.en: So when you're not quite sure what you should be doing, or you don't want to step on the toes of others, there can be a lot of energy that gets used up there with decision
sentences.zh: 当你不太确定自己应该做什么，或者不想越俎代庖时，在决策方面会消耗大量的精力，

sentences.en: making and trying to work out the best course of action.
sentences.zh: 并试图找出最佳行动方案。

sentences.en: When we don't have a control over our situation, or the resources available to us, or the demands being made, excessive criticism from others.
sentences.zh: 当我们无法控制自己的处境、可用的资源或被提出的要求时，来自他人的过度批评。

sentences.en: This is a really tricky one, again, that can feel like it's beyond our control.
sentences.zh: 这也是一个非常棘手的问题，同样会让人觉得超出了我们的控制范围。

sentences.en: And it links into the next one, which is lack of positive feedback or appreciation.
sentences.zh: 它与下一个问题有关，即缺乏积极的反馈或赞赏。

sentences.en: So if we're doing all of this work, but without this extra of people noticing and
sentences.zh: 所以如果我们做了所有这些工作，但没有这种额外的人们注意到并

sentences.en: seeing what we're doing, when there's any insecurity in our life, so uncertainty can really drain us.
sentences.zh: 看到我们在做什么，当我们的生活中出现任何不安全感时，不确定性真的会消耗我们。

sentences.en: So job insecurity, not knowing how long we're going to be in a post or having to continually reapply for work.
sentences.zh: 所以工作不安全感，不知道我们要在一个岗位上待多久，或者不得不不断地重新申请工作。

sentences.en: This is really hard for us.
sentences.zh: 这对我们来说真的很难。

sentences.en: Complex tasks, or a lot of complex tasks.
sentences.zh: 复杂的任务，或大量的复杂任务。

sentences.en: So we can't just kind of automate out certain things and kind of just know this is how I'm always doing things.
sentences.zh: 所以我们不能只是把某些事情自动化，或者仅仅知道这就是我一直做事的方式。

sentences.en: If we haven't to always wrap our head around more complexity and new instructions, this is really, again, an external
sentences.zh: 如果我们不得不总是去理解更多的复杂性和新的指令，这同样是来自我们所做工作类型的外部

sentences.en: pressure coming in at us from the type of work that we're doing.
sentences.zh: 压力。

sentences.en: Of course, last but not least is financial worries.
sentences.zh: 当然，最后但同样重要的是财务担忧。

sentences.en: So a lot of external pressures are visible and obvious, but not always.
sentences.zh: 所以很多外部压力是可见且明显的，但并非总是如此。

sentences.en: There can be some cultural ideals or ways that we expect men, women, carers to behave in a certain way that can also add to the type of external pressure certain people are under.
sentences.zh: 可能存在一些文化理想，或者我们期望男性、女性、照护者以某种特定方式行事的方式，这也可能增加某些人所承受的外部压力类型。

sentences.en: I go into this in chapter seven in my book.
sentences.zh: 我在书的第七章中深入探讨了这一点。

sentences.en: But I just want to introduce that idea right now that not all external pressures are easy to put your finger on.
sentences.zh: 但我现在只想介绍这个想法，即并非所有的外部压力都容易被察觉。

sentences.en: Some of them might just be almost an expectation that you kind of don't recognize that this could be something that you question or hold at arm's length to look at and
sentences.zh: 其中一些可能只是一种期望，你可能没有意识到这可能是你可以质疑或保持距离去审视的事情，并

sentences.en: decide actually, is this something that I do need to always be responding to?
sentences.zh: 决定实际上，这是我需要一直去回应的事情吗？

sentences.en: So some of these are really practical external pressures that we might be able to do something about.
sentences.zh: 所以其中一些是非常实际的外部压力，我们或许能够做些什么。

sentences.en: Sometimes we do have more control than we realize and we stop and spend some time working on what those options are to
sentences.zh: 有时我们拥有的控制权比我们意识到的要多，如果我们停下来花点时间研究一下有哪些选择来

sentences.en: reduce external pressures, then that's a really valuable piece of work.
sentences.zh: 减少外部压力，那将是一项非常有价值的工作。

sentences.en: But there are some external pressures that are less visible to us.
sentences.zh: 但有些外部压力对我们来说不太明显。

sentences.en: And they can often come from ideas that are woven into our culture.
sentences.zh: 它们通常来自植根于我们文化中的观念。

sentences.en: So for example, about our roles, what's expected from us, for example, that's different for
sentences.zh: 例如，关于我们的角色，对我们有什么期望，例如，这对

sentences.en: men and women, it might also be different depending on your role in the family, your role at work.
sentences.zh: 男性和女性是不同的，也可能根据你在家庭中的角色、在工作中的角色而有所不同。

sentences.en: So for example, women as carers, men as breadwinners, that's a very common one that most people can see as really unhelpful.
sentences.zh: 例如，女性作为照护者，男性作为养家糊口的人，这是一个非常普遍的观点，大多数人都能看出这是非常无益的。

sentences.en: And I go into this in one of the chaps in my book trying to help people understand the narratives that might underlie all of this.
sentences.zh: 我在书中的一章里深入探讨了这一点，试图帮助人们理解可能潜藏在这一切之下的叙事。

sentences.en: But just know for now that there are very obvious visible external pressures that we might be able to do something about.
sentences.zh: 但现在只要知道，有一些非常明显的可见外部压力，我们或许能够做些什么。

sentences.en: And there are others that are harder for us to fight on our own.
sentences.zh: 还有一些是我们自己更难对抗的。

sentences.en: And actually, this takes collective understanding and action to challenge.
sentences.zh: 实际上，这需要集体的理解和行动来挑战。

sentences.en: The second type of pressure is internal.
sentences.zh: 第二种压力是内部压力。

sentences.en: And this comes from pressures inside us, such as our emotions and our thoughts.
sentences.zh: 这来自我们内心的压力，例如我们的情绪和思想。

sentences.en: This can motivate us on through stress, even when we're feeling really quite tired, and we don't have much more to give.
sentences.zh: 即使在我们感到非常疲惫、没有更多精力付出时，这也能激励我们继续承受压力。

sentences.en: It can be informed partly by our biological and psychological makeup, such as our personality traits, core beliefs, any sensitivity to stimuli and temperament.
sentences.zh: 它部分受到我们生物学和心理构成的影响，例如我们的人格特质、核心信念、对刺激的敏感度和气质。

sentences.en: And it tends to show up as things like emotions, guilt, anxiety, shame, thoughts, such as, well, I'm responsible for keeping everything together, or we've not done
sentences.zh: 它往往表现为情绪、内疚、焦虑、羞耻，以及诸如“好吧，我有责任维持一切运转”或“我们还没有做

sentences.en: enough yet to deserve a break.
sentences.zh: 足够多来获得休息的资格”之类的想法。

sentences.en: And also unpleasant sensations in the body, which are linked to stress, such as that rush of adrenaline, everything then feels urgent, muscles are tense, your heart's racing,
sentences.zh: 还有身体上与压力相关的不愉快感觉，例如肾上腺素激增，一切都感觉很紧急，肌肉紧张，心跳加速，

sentences.en: you feel fidgety.
sentences.zh: 你感到坐立不安。

sentences.en: The idea of trying to pause or slow down just seems to go against what your nervous system is telling you.
sentences.zh: 试图暂停或放慢速度的想法似乎与你的神经系统告诉你的背道而驰。

sentences.en: In my book, I talk about three patterns of internal pressures that I see a lot in burnout in my work.
sentences.zh: 在我的书中，我谈到了我在工作中经常看到的倦怠中的三种内部压力模式。

sentences.en: So the first is people pleasing.
sentences.zh: 第一种是讨好型人格。

sentences.en: So obviously, being nice and kind to people isn't bad in and of itself.
sentences.zh: 显然，对人友善和仁慈本身并没有错。

sentences.en: But people pleasing is when it tips into feeling like you're worthless unless others are happy, your needs are bottom of the pile.
sentences.zh: 但讨好型人格是指当它演变成一种感觉，即除非别人快乐，否则你就是毫无价值的，你的需求被排在最后。

sentences.en: And so all of the thoughts and emotions and internal sensations are linked to that.
sentences.zh: 所以所有的思想、情绪和内在感觉都与此相关。

sentences.en: If you have any sense that others aren't feeling okay about things that you're doing, you will feel an urge to fix that and people pleasing.
sentences.zh: 如果你感觉到别人对你所做的事情不满意，你就会产生一种去修复它并讨好他们的冲动。

sentences.en: The second is perfectionism.
sentences.zh: 第二种是完美主义。

sentences.en: Again, the wish to do things well isn't in and of itself a bad thing.
sentences.zh: 同样，希望把事情做好本身并不是一件坏事。

sentences.en: It's when this tips into an exhausting pursuit of perfection at the expense of your well-being.
sentences.zh: 当它演变成以牺牲你的幸福为代价去追求完美的精疲力竭时，问题就出现了。

sentences.en: So not resting and not pausing and never delegating for fear of others getting things wrong.
sentences.zh: 所以不休息、不暂停，并且因为担心别人把事情搞砸而从不授权。

sentences.en: And this is usually fueled from a negative place, fearing the worst if you don't get things just so that others will reject you or you'll be criticized or put down.
sentences.zh: 这通常源于一种消极的心态，担心如果事情做得不够完美，最坏的情况会发生，比如别人会拒绝你，或者你会受到批评或贬低。

sentences.en: And so again, the internal pressures will tend to revolve around specific worry thoughts about exactly that, what will happen if things aren't perfect.
sentences.zh: 所以同样，内部压力往往会围绕着关于到底会发生什么的具体担忧想法，如果事情不完美的话。

sentences.en: And you get all of the internal sensations linked to moving on, always keeping your foot on the gas.
sentences.zh: 你会得到所有与继续前进、总是保持脚踩油门相关的内在感觉。

sentences.en: Third pattern that I go into in my book is this avoidance of emotions by using busyness.
sentences.zh: 我在书中深入探讨的第三种模式是通过忙碌来逃避情绪。

sentences.en: So if you fear your own body, you fear your own emotions, which can be, you know, really common.
sentences.zh: 所以如果你害怕自己的身体，害怕自己的情绪，这可能是，你知道，非常普遍的。

sentences.en: Negative emotions are really unpleasant.
sentences.zh: 负面情绪确实非常令人不快。

sentences.en: As we know, pretty much a lot of our work in psychology is about helping people develop a more compassionate relationship with their emotions.
sentences.zh: 正如我们所知，心理学中很大一部分工作是帮助人们与自己的情绪建立一种更具同情心的关系。

sentences.en: But it's really understandable that we would try and avoid negativity.
sentences.zh: 但我们试图逃避负面情绪是非常可以理解的。

sentences.en: And when we haven't had experience growing up of this, building up our confidence in our ability to be attuned and respond to our body, this can cause
sentences.zh: 当我们成长过程中没有这方面的经验，没有建立起对自己能够感知并回应身体能力的信心时，这可能会导致

sentences.en: people to overuse work as a strategy.
sentences.zh: 人们过度使用工作作为一种策略。

sentences.en: And so you might have these internal thoughts of I can't cope with negative anxiety or other emotions.
sentences.zh: 所以你可能会有这样的内心想法：我无法应对负面焦虑或其他情绪。

sentences.en: What if this tips me into a really difficult place I can never come back from.
sentences.zh: 如果这让我陷入一个我永远无法回头的非常困难的境地怎么办？

sentences.en: So I hope this is helpful for separating it out, beginning to think about what are the areas where I have control?
sentences.zh: 所以我希望这有助于将其区分开来，开始思考哪些领域是我可以控制的？

sentences.en: Yes, there are some areas of external pressures that I might benefit from stopping and trying to problem solve, maybe getting some support with.
sentences.zh: 是的，有些外部压力领域我可能通过停下来尝试解决问题，或许寻求一些支持会受益。

sentences.en: And that might involve practical and investment as well to try and get external pressures down.
sentences.zh: 这可能也涉及实际和投入，以试图降低外部压力。

sentences.en: And then there are internal pressures that is more role of self improvement and self healing.
sentences.zh: 然后还有内部压力，这更多是自我提升和自我疗愈的角色。

sentences.en: And, you know, the role of a psychologist can help with this.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，心理学家的角色可以帮助解决这个问题。

sentences.en: Again, absolutely, these areas are things that we can do something about.
sentences.zh: 同样，绝对地，这些领域是我们能够做些什么的事情。

sentences.en: But you've got to be aware of what your internal patterns are, and know how to slow it all down before responding before you do that.
sentences.zh: 但你必须意识到你的内在模式是什么，并知道在做出回应之前如何放慢速度。

sentences.en: So possibly reading my book, if you've got time or listening to it on audible or doing any of your own continued work that you might already have up your
sentences.zh: 所以，如果时间允许，可以读读我的书，或者在 Audible 上听，或者做任何你可能已经准备好的持续工作，

sentences.en: sleeve, like your mindfulness practices, or any other therapeutic approaches, compassion, focus
sentences.zh: 比如你的正念练习，或任何其他治疗方法，同情心聚焦

sentences.en: therapy and acts, these are all really, really helpful for trying to move through these patterns in a way or change your relationship with them.
sentences.zh: 疗法和 ACT，这些对于尝试以某种方式克服这些模式或改变你与它们的关系都非常有帮助。

sentences.en: I really hope you found this series of six episodes on burnout helpful.
sentences.zh: 我真心希望你觉得这六集关于倦怠的系列节目很有帮助。

sentences.en: I'd love to connect with you in my social media.
sentences.zh: 我很乐意在社交媒体上与你建立联系。

sentences.en: If you would like to find me, I'm on Instagram,
sentences.zh: 如果你想找到我，我在 Instagram 上，

sentences.en: I'm on TikTok, I'm on Facebook and LinkedIn.
sentences.zh: 我在 TikTok、Facebook 和 LinkedIn 上。

sentences.en: You can also, like I say, check out my book.
sentences.zh: 正如我所说，你也可以看看我的书。

sentences.en: And if you're on my mailing list, I love to get replies.
sentences.zh: 如果你在我的邮件列表中，我很喜欢收到回复。

sentences.en: So do check out my mailing list, you can access that via the website.
sentences.zh: 所以一定要看看我的邮件列表，你可以通过网站访问它。

sentences.en: All of the links to these are in the show notes.
sentences.zh: 所有这些链接都在节目说明中。

sentences.en: And I will now hand you back to Marianne, who is going to bring you her next episode, as usual, the slightly longer episodes that you are more accustomed to.
sentences.zh: 现在我把话筒交回给玛丽安，她将一如既往地为大家带来下一期节目，也就是你们更习惯收听的稍长篇幅的节目。

sentences.en: Thank you very much for having me and Marianne, thank you for allowing me this platform.
sentences.zh: 非常感谢你们邀请我，玛丽安，谢谢你为我提供这个平台。

sentences.en: Oh, thank you so much, Claire.
sentences.zh: 哦，非常感谢你，克莱尔。

sentences.en: And it's been lovely having you head up the podcast for this last six weeks.
sentences.zh: 过去六周由你来主持这档播客真是太棒了。

sentences.en: And you've done a beautiful job.
sentences.zh: 你做得非常出色。

sentences.en: So thank you for sharing so generously with my audience.
sentences.zh: 所以，感谢你如此慷慨地与我的听众分享。

sentences.zh: 也请我的听众朋友们，如果你们觉得这些内容有用，请务必加入克莱尔的

sentences.en: mailing liSt. And of course, grab your copy of burnout, how to manage your nervous system before it manages you.
sentences.zh: 邮件列表。当然，也别忘了买一本《倦怠：如何在神经系统掌控你之前先掌控它》。

sentences.en: Dr. Marianne Trent.
sentences.zh: 玛丽安·特伦特博士。

sentences.zh: 欢迎在Instagram、TikTok以及所有这些很棒的平台上关注我。

sentences.en: Don't forget that we have Marianne's motivation and mindset sessions, which happen weekly for free, exclusively in the free Facebook group.

sentences.en: And if you love what we do here on the podcast, I think you will adore what we do in the aspiring psychologist membership.

sentences.en: If you would like to access that, you can do for just £30 a month with no minimum term.

sentences.en: Collective and the Aspiring Psychologist Collective, please do drop me some ratings and reviews on Amazon and on Goodreads.

sentences.en: I am so privileged that you are part of my world and I will look forward to bringing
sentences.zh: 能让你成为我世界的一部分，我感到非常荣幸，我很期待为你带来

sentences.zh: 再次感谢。

sentences.zh: 我很期待很快见到你。

sentences.zh: 不，剧透一下，我当时并不是在教普拉提。
